title: Cleaned DATA file: slfs_essa_financial_merged_thru2025.csv
section: ESSA/SLFS (School-Level Finance Survey) Special Ed Spending info:
text:
ESSA/SLFS (School-Level Finance Survey) Special Ed Spending info:

It reflects direct classroom instruction (A2250 operating lines and F2250 school-age IDEA Part B grant lines).
It excludes four major special education spending areas: Out-of-District Tuition & Placements (Categorized under “Exclusions”): A2250.471: Public school district tuition A2250.472: Approved private 853 school and Special Act district tuition A2250.473: Direct special education payments to charter schools Why excluded: These tuition checks are stripped out of school building totals so they do not artificially distort individual school per-pupil averages. Special Education Transportation (Categorized under “Transportation”): General Fund Busing: Special education bus drivers/monitors (A5510.160/.161), contracted vendors (A5510.400), and BOCES busing (A5581.49) Summer ESY Busing: Section 4408 July/August special education transit (F5511, F5541, F5582) Related Services & Central Administration (Categorized under “Instructional Support” or “Central Overhead”): School Psychologists (A2820): Evaluators, test protocols, and certified psychologist salaries School Social Workers (A2825): Certified social workers and counseling services Pupil Personnel Services Directors (A2830): Special education administrators and central PPS office staff Special Education Legal Counsel (A1420.400): Retainers, attorneys, and impartial hearing costs (charged to central board legal) Summer Extended School Year Programs (Categorized under “Summer Programs”): F2253: July/August Section 4408 summer special education instructional costs
It also excludes: School legal spending
The website has a spreadsheet to show each ST3 code that’s included as SLSF “Special Ed”

title: Open School Data (NY)
text:
This website contains free, printable plots and visualizations of public data related to student literacy outcomes in our NY public schools.
We hope to help parents, teachers, and community members work together to help make needed change so all students learn to read and write in our public schools.
If you’d like to contribute, and care more about improving equity and student outcomes over profiting off of them, your ideas and contributions are welcome!
**DISCLAIMER: Nothing on this page should be construed as legal advice.
Use at your own discretion, and verify data - mistakes happen, please email any issues.
